source.title: Spectral Entropy Collapse as a Phase Transition in Delayed Generalisation: An Interventional and Predictive Framework for Grokkin
source.authors: Xuan Khanh Truong; Truong Quynh Hoa; Trung Duc Luu; D. Phan

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports grokking results on modular arithmetic using a 1-layer Transformer and says its setup follows Power et al. exactly; it also gives a paper-exact replication on the addition task. Its entropy, intervention, and Fourier measurements are additional tests of mechanisms behind the reproduced behaviour.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own training and test accuracy, entropy, intervention, and Fourier-alignment results. Literature findings it cites are not recorded as rows. The text does not vary training-set size within a task to test whether smaller sets increase the delay.
record.test_reason: The paper trains a 1-layer Transformer on (a+b) mod 97 with AdamW and weight decay 1.0, stating it follows Power et al. exactly. It reports delayed generalisation after memorisation on four algorithmic tasks (V1). It also tracks continuous measures, spectral entropy and Fourier alignment, that change gradually before the jump (V2). Its entropy-mixing interventions and norm-matched control concern the authors' own construct, not any version's mechanism.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors say spectral entropy collapse is the proximate, predictive and interventionally supported signal preceding grokking in 1-layer Transformers on group tasks. They say it is necessary but not sufficient, since the MLP collapses without grokking. They explicitly do not claim a fully causal effect, a universal threshold, or architectural necessity. They also claim entropy collapse, rather than parameter norm, is the primary driver of the delay. This rests on the norm-matched mixing control, which they acknowledge may have side effects on gradient flow and AdamW statistics.
record.recipe_differences: The paper says the 1-layer Transformer setup follows Power et al. exactly and includes paper-exact addition-task seeds. It adds spectral-entropy monitoring, representation mixing, norm matching, Fourier-alignment measurements, and an S5 task.
record.method_sensitivity: The threshold varies by task: H̃* is reported as 0.605 for addition, 0.589 for multiplication and subtraction, and 0.655 for S5. The paper also reports that entropy collapse without Fourier alignment in the MLP does not yield grokking.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixing penultimate representations (α=0.1) prevents entropy collapse and delays grokking by 5,020 steps (p=0.044). With norms rescaled to the baseline trajectory, the delay is 8,304 steps (28/30 seeds grokked, p=5e-5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Disrupting representation-covariance entropy collapse delays grokking independently of parameter norm.

record.problems: Main experiments use 10 seeds, and the authors give a wide 95% Clopper–Pearson interval for 10/10 threshold crossings ([69.2%, 100%]). The power-law fit explains R2 = 0.543 of variance, with the authors attributing remaining variance to stochasticity and unmodelled factors. The authors acknowledge possible intervention side effects on gradient flow, AdamW second-moment estimates, and attention softmax; the intervention does not isolate entropy from all training-dynamical covariates. The MLP comparison indicates entropy collapse is not sufficient.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible reported results were left out.

untested.parts: No within-task variation of training-set size, so the claim that the delay grows as data shrinks is untested.
No tracking of memorising components or their later removal (cleanup). Fourier alignment is measured only for addition.
Not tested: no non-algorithmic data and no initialisation-scale or lazy-to-rich manipulation.
Not tested: no LLM pretraining or fine-tuning.
Not tested: no weight-decay sweep, circuit-efficiency measure, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
Not tested: one architecture and hyperparameter set only. The cross-seed manifold in Fig 10 does not identify the algorithm across settings.
Not tested: no optimizer or softmax-precision manipulation.

missing.what: Predictor comparison: the entropy gap gives R2 0.507, versus 0.074 for parameter norm and negative values for loss and velocity predictors. Norm–entropy correlation is ρ=−0.248. This bears on which continuous progress measures anticipate the jump.
After grokking, entropy keeps declining slowly in all 10 seeds and Fourier alignment plateaus around 0.62. This describes continued post-grok refinement, loosely related to a cleanup phase.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V5 'challenges' label is removed. Matching norms under an entropy intervention, with weight decay unchanged, does not test the efficiency or critical-dataset-size account. The record's V2 'limits_scope' label is also removed: R9 is an induced intervention on the authors' own construct, and R11 is consistent with V2. The work is a preprint and the authors disclose heavy LLM assistance. Some internal numbers vary between sections: MAPE 4.1% vs 3.21%, and R2 0.543 vs 0.507.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not compare training-set sizes within a task, so it does not test whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks.

It measures gradual entropy reduction and Fourier alignment, and tests an entropy-disrupting intervention. It does not directly track removal of memorizing components or show that a specific circuit is removed later.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep, or lazy-to-rich transition test is reported.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning experiment is reported.
The norm-matched intervention tests parameter norm as a driver of delay, but the study does not measure circuit efficiency or test a critical dataset size or ungrokking below it.
The paper reports a consistent Fourier-alignment trend across seeds, but does not establish that runs converge to the same identifiable algorithm across architectures or hyperparameters.
Float64 is used for entropy computation, but the study does not test whether adaptive-optimizer instabilities or softmax numerical limits produce or eliminate grokking.

rows.subject: 1-layer Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Train on (a + b) mod 97 with AdamW and evaluate training and test accuracy.
rows.measure: Training and test accuracy over training steps; grokking at test accuracy ≥ 0.99.
rows.baseline: Test accuracy remains near chance after training accuracy reaches 1.0.
rows.value: Training accuracy reaches 1.0 within ≈ 500 steps; test accuracy remains near chance for thousands of steps before jumping to 1.0. Mean Tgrok = 14,360 steps (95% CI: [12,140, 17,100]).
rows.uncertainty: Mean Tgrok 95% CI: [12,140, 17,100]; Figure 1 reports mean ± 1.96 SE over 10 seeds.
rows.note: The text explicitly describes this as the classic grokking pattern. It does not test the effect of reducing the training fraction.

rows.subject: 1-layer Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Measure representation spectral entropy during training and compare its threshold crossing with the grokking step.

conditions.value: Fixed 512-example training-set probe; evaluated every 200 steps

rows.measure: Whether H̃ crosses H̃* before test accuracy ≥ 0.99, and lead time.
rows.value: H̃* = 0.609 (95% CI: [0.595, 0.624]); threshold crossing preceded test accuracy ≥ 0.99 in 10/10 runs, with mean lead time 1,020 steps (95% CI: [890, 1,140]).
rows.uncertainty: 95% CI for threshold [0.595, 0.624]; lead-time 95% CI [890, 1,140]; 10/10 crossing has exact Clopper–Pearson 95% CI [69.2%, 100%].
rows.note: The study defines collapse using a decrease of more than 0.05 over a 5-step rolling window.
rows.check: The 10/10 precedence result is Tcollapse < Tgrok, where Tcollapse is a rolling-window drop of more than 0.05. It is not H̃ crossing H̃*. H̃* itself is defined as H̃ at Tgrok, so 'crossing precedes grokking' is partly true by construction. Section 5 reports 10 seeds on addition, not three tasks × 10 seeds.

source_check.correct: Section 5 reports Tcollapse < Tgrok in 10/10 baseline seeds; Tcollapse is the first evaluation with an entropy decrease >0.05 over a five-evaluation rolling window. Mean lead: 1,020 steps, 95% CI [890, 1,140]. H̃*=H̃(Tgrok) averages 0.609, 95% CI [0.595, 0.624]. The baseline is addition modulo 97 with 10 seeds; the separate add/mul/sub universality experiments use 5 seeds each.
source_check.locator_found: Sections 4–5, Figures 1–2; Section 9, Table 3; Appendix A, Table 5.
source_check.problem: Conflates rolling-window collapse with point-threshold crossing and combines the 10-seed baseline with the three-task, five-seed-per-task experiments.

rows.subject: 1-layer Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Fit and evaluate a power-law predictor based on the entropy gap to grokking.
rows.measure: Prediction of remaining training time until grokking from H̃ − H̃*.
rows.value: R2 = 0.543 (95% CI: [0.513, 0.573]); γ = 1.65; reported mean absolute percentage error = 4.1% and mean lead time = 12,370 steps.
rows.uncertainty: R2 95% CI: [0.513, 0.573]; reported 95% predictive interval approximately ±6,000 steps.
rows.note: The paper separately reports leave-one-out MAPE at Tgrok − 1 of 3.21% (median 1.69%, maximum 14.55% across 10 held-out seeds).

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.3, Corollary 1; Section 8, Figure 5 and leave-one-out prediction paragraph.

rows.subject: GrokTransformer (paper-exact 1-layer Transformer)
rows.size_stated: 1-layer Transformer; dmodel not restated in this section
rows.operation_detail: Measure spectral entropy and Fourier alignment during training.
rows.measure: Pre-grokking Pearson correlation between H̃ and AFourier; trajectories of both measures.
rows.value: Mean seed-level correlation ρ̄ = −0.82 (range [−0.86, −0.76]); H̃ decreases while AFourier rises during entropy collapse, with AFourier rising from ≈ 0.25 to ≈ 0.62 in Phase II.
rows.note: The authors interpret the coupled measures as gradual formation of a Fourier-aligned representation. They do not directly identify or track removal of memorizing components.

rows.subject: 1-layer Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Mix representations across the batch during training to prevent entropy collapse.
rows.measure: Mean grokking step and delay relative to baseline.
rows.value: Intervention mean Tgrok = 19,420; delay = +5,020 steps; 10/10 seeds grokked.
rows.note: The authors state that mixing prevents H̃ from collapsing below H̃* and acknowledge possible effects on gradient flow and AdamW second-moment estimates.
rows.check: An induced representation-mixing intervention on the authors' entropy construct. It does not measure circuit formation, memorisation removal, or any version's named mechanism. Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: 1-layer Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Keep representation mixing active while rescaling weight norms to match the baseline trajectory.

conditions.value: Rescaled to exactly match baseline norm trajectory

rows.measure: Mean grokking step and delay relative to baseline.
rows.value: 28/30 seeds grokked; mean Tgrok = 22,664; delay = +8,304 steps.
rows.note: The authors interpret this norm-matched result as evidence that entropy collapse, rather than parameter norm, is the primary driver of delay in their setting. Two seeds did not cross H̃* within 50,000 steps.
rows.check: The norm-matched control rescales norms while mixing stays on, and weight decay of 1.0 remains throughout. It tests neither whether a low-norm bias favours a more efficient circuit, nor a critical dataset size, nor ungrokking. It does not bear on V5. Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: MLP
rows.operation_detail: Train on modular arithmetic and measure training accuracy, test accuracy, spectral entropy, and Fourier alignment.
rows.measure: Test accuracy after training accuracy saturates and H̃ collapses.
rows.baseline: Test accuracy near zero before and throughout the reported training horizon.
rows.value: Training accuracy reaches 1.0; H̃ drops from 0.76 to 0.15, below H̃* = 0.609; test accuracy remains near zero for 80,000 steps. Maximum Fourier alignment |r| = 0.052.
rows.note: This is a counterexample to entropy collapse being sufficient for generalisation; the authors say the MLP’s Fourier alignment remains near zero.
rows.check: Relinked from V2 to V1. An MLP on modular arithmetic (p=41) memorises but never generalises within 80,000 steps, so delayed grokking is absent for this architecture. MLP hyperparameters are not stated. Low Fourier alignment alongside no generalisation is consistent with V2 rather than limiting it.

rows.subject: 1-layer Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Train on the same task as the MLP comparison and measure grokking.
rows.measure: Test accuracy following H̃ threshold crossing.
rows.baseline: Test accuracy before grokking is near zero.
rows.value: Grokking occurs at step 1,600 after a memorisation plateau; H̃ crosses H̃* and generalisation follows.
rows.note: Presented as a comparator to the MLP trained on the same task.
rows.check: Relinked from V2 to V1. The Transformer at p=41 groks at step 1,600 after a memorisation plateau. Seed count and exact delay relative to memorisation are not stated.

reader_labels.reason: Mixing delays but does not eliminate grokking, and the MLP shows entropy collapse without generalisation; entropy collapse alone is therefore not sufficient in the tested settings (R9, R11).

reader_labels.reason: Grokking remains substantially delayed when weight norms are matched to baseline, which the authors take as evidence against parameter norm being the primary driver in this setting (R10).
